title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a proof. The setting is a smooth projective variety X of dimension n with a Weil cohomology H*. ξ is the hyperplane (Lefschetz) class acting by cup product. P^i is the primitive part of H^i. A is the algebra of algebraic correspondences, i.e. the operators induced by algebraic cycle classes on X×X. T_k is the Künneth projector onto H^k. u_m : H^{2n-m} → H^m is the inverse of the hard Lefschetz isomorphism ξ^{n-m} : H^m → H^{2n-m}, assumed (or already shown) to lie in A. This is the content of Lefschetz-type standard conjecture B.

The operator under study is ξ^j u_{k-2j} ξ^{n-k+j} T_k on H^k. Use the Lefschetz decomposition H^k = ⊕_{i'+2j'=k} ξ^{j'} P^{i'} and take x ∈ P^{i'}.
- ξ^{n-k+j}(ξ^{j'} x) = ξ^{n-k+j+j'} x.
- This is nonzero exactly when n-k+j+j' ≤ n-i', i.e. j ≤ j'. Primitive classes of degree i' are killed by ξ^{n-i'+1}.
- When j' ≥ j, the element lies in ξ^{n-(k-2j)}(H^{k-2j}). Applying u_{k-2j} gives ξ^{j'-j} x, and then ξ^j returns ξ^{j'} x.

So the composite is exactly the projection of H^k onto ξ^j H^{k-2j} = ⊕_{j'≥j} ξ^{j'} P^{i'}, along the components with j' < j. All factors are in A, so this projection is in A.

Now argue by descending induction on j. The partial projections onto ξ^{j'} P^{i'} for j' > j are in A. Their sum is the projection onto ξ^{j+1} H^{k-2j-2}. Taking the difference shows that the projection onto ξ^j P^i (i = k-2j) is in A. This proves the lemma: under the Lefschetz standard conjecture, the projectors onto the primitive components of the Lefschetz decomposition are algebraic. This is a step toward the algebraicity of the Hodge * operator and Λ, and the positivity (Hodge-type) conjecture in the Poincaré–Hodge algebra formalism.

The neighbouring pages (Bourbaki 'Tribu n° 65', étale algebras) are unrelated archival material.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'par différence' step implicitly uses descending induction on j, starting from the top j where ξ^j H^{k-2j} = ξ^j P^{k-2j}; this is not stated on this page but is standard.
